Crypto counts as confirmed only once the gateway reports the required confirmations. Manual gateways (bank, Wise) keep staff review (approve/reject). hold_hours (whole hours, the console field) can only lengthen the wait: on an automatic gateway a value above 0 holds the payment that many hours instead of 10 minutes; on a manual gateway it is the review window after which the dashboard flags the payment.

extra.conflict: A merchant's fixed custom price stays fixed when the supplier raises its price (the Dhru behaviour a merchant pointed out). The floor used services.cost, which changes only when the admin imports changed items (M96), so orders could be sold below the new supplier cost until then.
extra.decision: User decision (2026-10-31). (1) Effective cost at order time = max(services.cost, the latest synced cost of the service's first active supplier link, credit x credit_rate in USD); floor = effective cost + minimum profit (RULES services 1); an order pays max(resolved price, floor) as before, so a fixed client or group price can no longer sell below a raised supplier cost. The supplier sync updates it at once; importing changed items stays as it is (it updates services.cost and keeps cost_was). (2) Dashboard: services_below_floor uses the effective cost, so a supplier price rise shows right after the sync. (3) Price lists show the real price: Dhru imeiservicelist/serverservicelist/fileservicelist, the REST v1 catalog, the portal catalog and the price export resolve with the effective floor; a sync that changes an effective cost bumps the catalog price version (decision 022). (4) Price-change guard on merchant orders (Dhru, REST v1, portal): the backend keeps, per merchant and service, the last price it listed to them (with currency and time; written only when it changes). If the charged price exceeds that listed price by more than the setting pricing.price_change_tolerance_percent (default 10), the order is refused: 409 PRICE_CHANGED (problem+json with listedPrice and currentPrice) or, on the Dhru surface, ERROR "Price changed. Please refresh the service list and order again.". Up to the tolerance the new price is charged and the order's pricing_snapshot records listedPrice and raised = true with the reason (floor or price change). No listing on record: no check. (5) Notifications: when the resolved price of a service changes for a merchant who placed an order for it in the last 30 days, the merchant gets one digest per change batch (service, old and new price) by email and Telegram (their notification preferences) and the outgoing webhook event service.price_changed (a backend addition to the map's three events: route parity allows it under this B-entry). (6) Lead default, not part of the user's rule: dispatch never fails over to a supplier link whose cost is above the order's charged price; such an order goes to needs_attention. This applies to automatic failover only; a staff change-supplier or dispatch may use a costlier link (recorded as costAbovePrice, resolution orders-suppliers-12). Features: 4b (resolver, listed-price memory, guard, snapshot, setting), 6 (sync recomputes the effective cost, failover check), 7a (Dhru message, listing memory on every list action), 7b (service.price_changed), 9 (dashboard alert), 12a (template and digest job).

extra.decision: User decision (2026-11-01): the accounts are opened in the same DB transaction that creates the merchant. Feature 3 owns the public service `MerchantAccounts.open(tx, { clientId, currency: 'USD', creditLimit, overdraftAllowed })`, exported from src/modules/money/index.ts: raw inserts with ON CONFLICT (ledger_accounts_identity_uq) DO NOTHING of client_wallet (owner_type 'client', overdraft_limit = creditLimit ?? '0.0000') and client_hold (overdraft_limit 0); no postTransaction and no money event; it applies user rule 2 (creditLimit > 0 needs a group with overdraft_allowed, else 422 on creditLimit, the same answer as PATCH /admin/clients/:id/credit-limit) and returns the wallet view {balance '0.0000', reserved '0.0000', creditLimit, available}. POST /admin/clients (2a) calls it with the entered creditLimit; POST /client/auth/register (2b) calls it with creditLimit 0, so no merchant exists without accounts. 'Created on first use' stays only as a safety fallback. Order: feature 3 implements and merges first, 2a calls it; feature 3's seed creates the accounts of the demo merchants that 2a seeds. 2a reads the group (exists, kind not b2c_retail, overdraft_allowed) through a read-only ClientGroupDirectory in the catalog module's public index (4a extends it). Group moves keep the invariant: PATCH /admin/clients/:id {groupId} to a group without overdraft is 422 on groupId while the wallet's overdraft_limit is above 0, and in 4a switching a group's overdraft_allowed off is refused while any of its merchants has a limit above 0. A negative creditLimit stays 422 on creditLimit.

extra.decision: auth_tokens.purpose 'invite' with subject_type 'client', a hash only, expiry 1 hour like every one-time token (decisions 010/019). The link is `<PORTAL_BASE_URL>/set-password?token=<token>`, built from the new config key PORTAL_BASE_URL (the counterpart of the console base URL). 2a writes the token and the outbox event `merchant.invited` (ids only, never the token); until feature 12a adds the template, 2b's MailSender development implementation logs a redacted line. The consuming route is POST /client/auth/password/reset {token, password}, which accepts purposes 'reset' and 'invite': it sets password_hash (argon2id), password_changed_at = now and email_verified_at = now (the link proves the email), sets used_at, voids the merchant's other unused tokens and answers 204; it does not sign in. The status stays 'pending' until staff approve with PATCH /admin/clients/:id. A merchant who misses the hour uses POST /client/auth/password/forgot, which also works for a pending merchant with no password yet. auth_tokens.purpose is a closed vocabulary: CHECK auth_tokens_purpose_check purpose IN ('invite','reset','verify_email','magic_link'), from an exported AUTH_TOKEN_PURPOSES const in src/modules/identity/db/schema.ts (STAFF_TOKEN_PURPOSES is derived from it), shipped in the lead's single pre-wave-1 audit migration (0003).

extra.decision: Common rules of the merchant portal routes (ALIGNMENT § 3 and § 7, decision 018). Public routes (register, verify-email, login, password/forgot, password/reset) need no session and no CSRF token but are accepted only with an Origin header that is one of CORS_ORIGINS; pipeline order IP rules (403 IP_NOT_ALLOWED) → per-IP rate limit (429 RATE_LIMITED with Retry-After; login, 2fa and password routes have the strict limits) → handler. Session routes use the cookie gsm_client_session (httpOnly, Secure, SameSite=Lax, __Host- in production) and the readable CSRF cookie csrf_token_client; every mutation with a session sends X-CSRF-Token (403 CSRF_FAILED, never signs out); no active session is 401 UNAUTHORIZED. A sign-in creates a pending session (sessions.stage pending_totp, 10 minutes) when a second step is needed and an active one otherwise; reaching active rotates the token; lifetimes are the settings sessions.client_* (30 days absolute, 10080 minutes idle by default). Session-ending codes (401, 403 ACCOUNT_SUSPENDED, 403 IP_NOT_ALLOWED) are only ever about the caller, so a wrong current password or code is 422 on its field, never 401. Success statuses: one per route, bodies JSON or empty; lists are simple-rest. Cache-Control: no-store on /client/auth/* and on any response that carries a secret. Passwords follow the staff policy (at least 10 characters, not trivial: 422 WEAK_PASSWORD). One-time tokens (verify_email, reset, invite) are 1 hour, single use, hash only (decisions 010/019). Mails are outbox events with ids only (merchant.email_verification, merchant.password_reset, merchant.invited); 2b registers the processor that hands them to the MailSender interface. Merchant 2FA is optional TOTP (6 digits, plus or minus one step, a used step is never accepted twice: clients.totp_last_step), with clients.twofa_enabled false while the secret is only pending; the columns these specs need on clients (twofa_enabled, totp_last_step, password_changed_at) come with 2b's migration and a B116 note.

An existing email changes nothing and sends nothing. A gateway confirmation captures the payment even when it was already failed (an expired crypto payment confirmed late takes money, so it must end in an order or a refund). A second payment for one checkout is a duplicate: booked and refunded at once, never the order's payment, no receipt invoice. The order's payment is the one the approved refund names, else the one linked to the order's first receipt invoice. The receipt is rendered once after the capture commits (outbox event receipt.render on the files queue) and stored; downloads serve the stored bytes and render on the fly only when the stored copy is missing; the route lists 503 UNAVAILABLE. Refunds stay processing between the approval and the gateway's answer (user rule 7); the gateway call runs outside any transaction with the key refund-<id>, and refund-<id>-<n> once the gateway refused it for good (n = refunds.send_attempt, a schema addition with CHECK >= 1; a 4xx other than 408, 409, 425 and 429 fails the refund, a timeout or 5xx retries with the same key); a late refund.failed of an older attempt is logged and ignored (the attempt travels as gateway metadata), a late refund.succeeded still completes. A failed refund still counts against what is left on the payment until it is retried; approving with nothing left is 422 'Nothing is left to refund on this payment.'; approval locks the order, then the payment, then the refund. The storefront policy autoRefundFailed (default on) covers only rejections the system decides (a supplier's result): a staff rejection refunds at once, and with the policy off a system rejection opens a refund requested by the system (no journal) whose approval posts from customer funds. A sixteenth account kind customer_wallet (owner customer), one USD account per customer; no customer_hold account: a balance payment moves money to the pooled customer_funds like a card capture, and the wallet is closed loop (no cash-out, no expiry). The stored ref type 'customer' is sent as 'system' on /admin/ledger/*, and the console types the account kind as a string. Five wallet money events beyond the map's 13 reuse the kinds deposit, b2c_payment, refund, adjustment and chargeback (customer_topup, b2c_wallet_pay, b2c_wallet_refund, customer_adjust, topup_chargeback; their own id set WALLET_EVENT_IDS next to the map's 13); every one balances to zero and is tested. A debit that would take a customer wallet below zero is refused under the row lock (INSUFFICIENT_FUNDS); the one exception is the clawback of a lost top-up dispute. A freeze blocks paying from the balance and card top-ups; bank top-ups, credits, refunds and staff adjustments still work. Unfreeze is staff-only, 409 CONFLICT while the balance is negative and OPEN_DISPUTE while a dispute is open; a won dispute does not unfreeze. A freeze or unfreeze that changes nothing still writes an audit row (alreadyFrozen, alreadyUnfrozen). New error codes WALLET_FROZEN and WALLET_DISABLED.

extra.conflict: A storefront order could be paid by card, bank or crypto only. The wire value 'balance' on refunds and reports is B182; this entry is the payment itself and two checkout bugs found on the way.
extra.decision: Lead record (feature 21). Order payment method 'balance': payments.gateway_id is nullable for this method only, and there is at most one balance payment per checkout session. POST /store/v1/checkout-sessions/:token/balance-payment needs the checkout token and a signed-in customer session with its CSRF token (checked in the handler), a required Idempotency-Key (up to 255 characters, as /pay) and no body; it creates the order and takes the balance in one transaction and answers 201 { payment, order { id, trackingToken }, wallet }. A replay answers the first result with the wallet as it is now. 401 on this route means 'sign in to pay from the balance', not an ended session. A balance payment needs a checkout opened while signed in (checkout_sessions.opened_signed_in): a guest, or a link prepared for someone else, can never spend a balance. The session answers gain the additive boolean balancePayable (wallet on and the session opened signed in; never a balance, because the token is not an identity). VAT is booked at spend with the session's locked rate; a top-up invoice carries no tax and no PDF. Refunds go to where the money came from: balance-paid to the balance at once, card-paid to the card (no store credit); GET /admin/reports/vat is correct for both. Existing defect fixed: paymentMethods in the checkout session and in GET /store/v1/config now list only gateways that /pay accepts (a gateway with an unknown driver could never be paid).

extra.conflict: A chargeback on a customer's card top-up had no rule: webhooks for those payments were ignored and the map's dispute flow is built on an order.
extra.decision: Lead record (feature 21; reviewed by the lead). The payments webhook records top-ups of customer invoices, and the disputes webhook handles disputes of top-up payments for customers and merchants (before, dropped). dispute.created freezes the wallet. On a lost dispute the credited amount is clawed back pro rata and never more than the top-up's gross, the balance may go negative, the platform's fee income is reversed and the dispute fee is booked as a loss; staff collect or write off with an audited adjustment. The payment stays 'approved' and the dispute is shown on the deposit (Finance, Deposits) and on the customer's wallet view; GET /admin/disputes and its evidence screens still serve order disputes only. A top-up disputed before it was credited goes to review; if the dispute is lost the payment is rejected and its invoice voided. A dispute in another currency than its top-up takes the whole credit back and books no dispute fee (a fail-safe that is only logged; with today's drivers it cannot happen). A lost dispute with no recorded 'created' event is acknowledged and logged only. Admin payments (list, detail, approve, reject) gain customer { id, name, email, walletBalance } | null and dispute { id, status, reasonCode, amount, fee, evidenceDueAt, resolvedAt, transactionId } | null, and the list gains filters customerId and owner (merchant|customer) and searches customer name and email. Customer top-ups use the merchant memo and count 'first deposit' per customer (note 'First top-up of this customer.'). A cancelled top-up keeps its Idempotency-Key (a retry answers the cancelled top-up); one voided by a gateway failure frees it. The dashboard's 'disputes due' item counts order disputes only.

extra.conflict: A balance changes what the customer may see, what staff may erase and what mail the customer gets; the map has no rule for any of these.
extra.decision: Lead record (feature 21). The customer's statement never shows staff reasons: an adjustment reads 'Balance adjustment'. POST /admin/customers/:id/anonymize is refused with 409 CONFLICT while the wallet is not empty or money is in flight (an unpaid top-up, an unfinished balance-paid order); the customer data export gains wallet. Five customer mail events with English and Arabic templates: wallet.topup_credited, wallet.topup_rejected, wallet.adjusted, wallet.frozen, wallet.order_refunded. Known gap recorded by the money review: closeForErasure should also refuse while a balance-paid order is not final, since a later rejection would credit an anonymized wallet.

extra.conflict: Staff could approve, suspend or decline a merchant but could not help one who is locked out: no password link or temporary password, no 2FA reset, no end of sessions, no verification resend. These four routes are not in the map.
extra.decision: Lead record (feature 20). New permission clients:security (a role that holds clients:* gets it; in the dev seed Admin and Support); profile and status actions keep clients:update. Password (no-store): sends a link (purpose 'invite' while the merchant has no password, 'reset' when there is one; the older link answers 410) or sets a temporary password (14 characters, passes the policy, shown once, sets clients.must_change_password and cancels open links). Reset 2FA: 204, clears the three TOTP columns and ends a pending_totp session; 409 TWOFA_NOT_ENABLED when 2FA is off. Sessions revoke: 204, ends full and pending sessions (204 with none). Verification resend: 204; 409 CONFLICT when already verified; a suspended merchant is refused (a link for one is 410). A suspended merchant is 409 NOT_ACTIVE on the password routes. Mail limit: five mails per hour per account and kind (password link, verification, email change), for merchants and staff, 429 over; refused calls spend none. The merchant's own resend (POST /client/auth/verify-email/resend, see B193) shares the limiter. Not built: staff editing a merchant's notification preferences or unlinking Telegram.

extra.conflict: A merchant with a staff-set temporary password could sign in and use the portal with it; LEAD-DECISIONS said to mirror the staff forced-change flow, which ends every session after the change.
extra.decision: Lead record (feature 20). Merchants get a forced password change. Login answers next: 'password' when must_change_password is set (before the 2FA step), with a session in the new stage pending_password; every other merchant route refuses that stage, and only the change route and logout accept it. POST /client/auth/password/change takes { password } only, refuses a weak password and the temporary one (422 WEAK_PASSWORD on 'password', the flag stays), rotates the session (new cookie, old token dead) and answers { next: 'done' } or { next: 'totp' } when 2FA is on; POST /client/auth/2fa then still answers 204. Unlike the staff flow the merchant's sign-in continues after the change instead of ending every session, because the optional 2FA step must still follow and a second login adds nothing. Me gains mustChangePassword. POST /client/auth/verify-email/resend (merchant session, pending merchants allowed): 204, the older link becomes 410, 409 CONFLICT when verified. The owner decision stands: the order is password first, then the 2FA code.

extra.route: PATCH /admin/clients/:id, GET /admin/clients, GET /admin/clients/:id, merchant profile routes, suspend and reactivate
extra.conflict: Staff could not correct a merchant's details or email, the merchant row had no address, tax id, language or staff notes, and a suspension left password and verification links alive.
extra.decision: Lead record (feature 20). PATCH /admin/clients/:id takes details as a third kind of change beside profile and status (clients:update). Business information: address, taxId, locale (merchant and staff edit them) and internalNotes (staff only); invoices do not print address or tax id yet. Email change is staff only: sessions stay, every open link is cancelled, verification is cleared, a verification (or invitation) goes to the new address and the old address is not notified; an email another merchant has is 409 EMAIL_TAKEN, while one that a storefront customer also uses is allowed (the merchant wins on the smart sign-in, B208). The new keys on the merchant row and on the key row are optional on the wire (console fixtures are validated against the schema); the lead may make them required once the console's types carry them. Schema additions are in the style of B116. Suspension voids every open link, and pending to suspended is allowed: this is how an application is declined (reactivating such a merchant makes it active). API keys are not revoked on suspension: they are refused while suspended and work again after reactivation. Approval conditions are unchanged (neither a verified email nor an approved KYC is required).

extra.conflict: Only a merchant could make an API key; support had no way to issue one or change a key's limits. The two routes are not in the map.
extra.decision: Lead record (feature 20). POST /admin/clients/:id/api-keys (api_keys:create, no-store): only for an active merchant; the secret is shown once; api_keys.created_by records the staff member and the key row gains createdByStaff, so the merchant sees 'made by support' and is mailed. The 10-active-keys limit applies with the staff text 'This merchant already has 10 active keys'. PATCH /admin/api-keys/:id (api_keys:update): per-minute limit 1 to 6000 and allowed addresses (validated first); it also works on a key of a suspended merchant so staff can lower a limit during a suspension. Lock order, which overrides the plan: the advisory lock api-keys:<clientId> is taken before the clients row FOR UPDATE, because the merchant's own insert holds a key-share lock on the clients row while it holds the advisory lock; only the two creation paths take it.

extra.conflict: Merchants got no mail for approval, KYC results, suspension or reactivation, and staff invitations and reset links were not delivered by mail.
extra.decision: Lead record (feature 20). Six transactional merchant events, English and Arabic by clients.locale (every merchant mail uses it), email only and always sent: approval, KYC approved, KYC rejected (with the staff note), suspension (without the staff reason), reactivation, and a security notice (temporary password, 2FA reset, key made by staff). Staff mails: staff.invited and staff.password_reset deliver the invitation and reset link by email, with the staff token rotated in the job. CONSOLE_BASE_URL is required in production (add it to the 24D production env template and its allow-list test). The mail limit is the one of B192 (five an hour per account and kind).

extra.conflict: Staff actions on a merchant's records were not filed under the merchant, and the session list could not be narrowed to one account.
extra.decision: Lead record (feature 20). KYC decisions and the end of one merchant session by staff are audited under entity type 'merchant' (for example 'ended a session of'), so they appear in that merchant's history; the merchant's own actions are still not audited. GET /admin/sessions gains the filter subjectId, and subjectType is required beside it.

extra.route: GET|POST|PATCH|DELETE /admin/notification-campaigns*, GET /admin/inbox*, GET /client/notifications*, GET /store/v1/me/notifications*, POST /store/v1/marketing/unsubscribe/:token, GET /admin/notifications
extra.conflict: The map has a notification log and templates but no way to send an announcement to many people and no in-app inbox. The 25 routes below are not in the map.
extra.decision: Lead record (feature 23). Twenty-five routes beyond the map (scripts/map-additions/23.mjs, stage 23). Staff campaigns, 12 routes: list, create (201, status draft), get, PATCH, DELETE (drafts only, NOT_A_DRAFT), audience-preview, preview, test, send (202), schedule, cancel and recipients. New permission area broadcasts:read|send (read: list, get, previews, recipients; send: everything that writes or sends); only the Owner has it until a role is granted it, no extra permission for marketing and no second approval for large sends. Inbox, 12 routes, four per surface: admin (staff session) /admin/inbox, /unread-count, /:id/read, /read-all; merchant /client/notifications* (pending merchants may read); customer /store/v1/me/notifications*. Unsubscribe: POST /store/v1/marketing/unsubscribe/:token (see B202). Additive: GET /admin/notifications gains the filter campaignId and the row field campaignId (the console type has no such field, an info note in shape parity). Campaign and inbox writes by staff are audited, except the two staff read-state POSTs and the previews (audit: false with the reason).

extra.conflict: The map defines no campaign lifecycle, audience, content rule or send guard.
extra.decision: Lead record (feature 23). Status: 'sent' means the fan-out finished; delivery progress is in the detail's counters; a cancelled campaign's queued messages are logged 'failed' with the reason (no new log status), its in-app items are hidden and its rows take no send budget. A sent announcement cannot be retracted. Content is plain text (any HTML tag is refused), {{name}} is the only placeholder, 'en' is required and 'ar' optional with 'en' as fallback, and links are site-relative per audience; the in-app text of system events is defined in code, not editable by staff. A template for an untemplated event is refused with the field code not_templated under VALIDATION_FAILED. Audience: active staff, active merchants and active customers with an account; pending merchants are an option; a person who is both merchant and customer gets two messages (no merge by email). Send needs confirmRecipients, the 'reachable' number the staff member saw; a drift above max(5, 2 percent) is 409 CONFLICT. Send and schedule also move the row only if audience, channels and purpose still equal what was counted, otherwise 409 CONFLICT; a stored audience that no longer parses makes PATCH answer 422. Scheduling: a minute sweep, at least 1 minute ahead and at most 90 days, with reschedule and cancel (INVALID_TRANSITION from a final state).

extra.route: Tables notification_campaigns, notification_inbox, notifications.campaign_id; inbox routes
extra.conflict: The notification log's channel enum could not hold an in-app channel, and no store existed for per-person inbox items.
extra.decision: Lead record (feature 23). New tables notification_campaigns and notification_inbox (platform, additionalTables) and column notifications.campaign_id; the in-app channel is a table, not a value of the log's channel enum. In-app items are also created for the storefront order, payment and refund mails and for a merchant's low balance and paid invoice, but not for merchant order results. Inbox rules: the recipient always comes from the session actor, never from the path, query or body; another person's item id is 404 NOT_FOUND, never 403; mark-one-read is 204 and idempotent; mark-all-read takes optional upToId (so an item arriving during the click stays unread) and answers { updated }; the unread count answers { unread } capped at 100 (clients show 99+); list filter unread and locale, 100 per page; answers are never cached. Retention: read items 90 days, all items 365 days, the log 180 days, campaigns kept; the customer data export does not list inbox items; anonymization deletes them.

extra.conflict: Decision 020 had ten queues, and a broadcast of thousands of messages would starve transactional mail on the shared notifications queue and the SMTP and Telegram limits.
extra.decision: Lead record (feature 23; decision 020 amended). An eleventh queue notification-broadcasts, with its own queue limiter and per-channel budgets (documented in docs/queues.md); the notifications queue keeps no limiter. Default budgets are 5 emails and 20 Telegram messages per second, both editable settings, with a ceiling of 30 jobs per second; one SMTP account serves transactional and bulk mail. QueuesService gains addBulk. Fan-out runs in chunks with deterministic job ids; cancelling stops the next chunk; a Telegram 429 is retried inside the same attempt.

extra.route: POST /store/v1/marketing/unsubscribe/:token; recipient rules of every notification
extra.conflict: Mail to a suspended or blocked customer was dropped even for orders and payments, there was no marketing consent rule and no one-click unsubscribe.
extra.decision: Lead record (feature 23). Every campaign is purpose 'service' or 'marketing'. Marketing reaches only customers with marketing_opt_in and a granting latest consent record, on every channel, checked at fan-out and again at send; marketing email carries an unsubscribe link and one-click headers (RFC 8058). Merchants switch announcement email and Telegram off in their preferences (one event for both purposes; in-app always arrives); Telegram announcements are on by default for a merchant with a linked chat. POST /store/v1/marketing/unsubscribe/:token is public, CSRF-free and Turnstile-free by design (a mailbox provider calls it), takes the form body List-Unsubscribe=One-Click or no body, and answers 204 (also for an unknown or erased customer; it writes only consent); a token that does not verify is 410 TOKEN_INVALID; the token is a stateless 128-bit keyed HMAC. recipientOf reads the customer's status: anonymized customers get nothing, and six customer events plus support.ticket_received are transactional, so order, payment, refund and ticket mails keep reaching a suspended or blocked customer; the satisfaction survey no longer does.

extra.conflict: REST v1 orders accept an Idempotency-Key, the merchant portal's POST /client/orders did not, so a double click or a retry could place the order twice.
extra.decision: Lead record (feature 24B). POST /client/orders accepts an optional Idempotency-Key header (1 to 255 characters, printable ASCII) with REST v1's semantics under a new store scope 'portal' (idempotency_keys_scope_check widens to order, bulk, portal). The key is not written to orders.idempotency_key because a bulk makes several orders; the idempotency_keys row alone guards the portal, and the stored answer commits in the same transaction as the orders (the placement now runs as one transaction and reads the order views inside it). The first answer is 201 { orders }; a replay returns the same body plus the header idempotency-replayed: true; the same key with a different body is 409 IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED and a request still running is 409 IDEMPOTENCY_IN_PROGRESS with Retry-After. The header stays optional (existing callers unchanged), the idempotency window of 7 days and the daily purge (P4a follow-ups entry) apply to the new scope as to the others, and ALIGNMENT.md section 7 notes it.

extra.conflict: A customer could change their password and preferences but not their name, phone or country; the body refused them (D6 D-12 left email change open).
extra.decision: Lead record (feature 24B). PATCH /store/v1/me (full customer session, CSRF, no Turnstile) now also takes name (2 to 120), phone (up to 40, '' clears) and country (ISO-2), with the same rules as the staff edit; all fields optional and {} stays valid; answers 200 StoreMe; refusals are 422 on 'name', 'phone' or 'country'. A country change re-derives the currency unless the request sends one (an explicit currency wins); a country equal to the stored one is never checked; the check and derivation run inside the transaction on the locked row. No audit row for a customer's own edit. The customer still cannot change email (the owner decides whether that is allowed and whether the new address must be verified first). Still open and out of scope: tracking link in order mails, data-export delivery, orderable model, network and MEP options.

extra.route: Card gateway driver (Stripe protocol), POST /webhooks/payments/:gateway, POST /store/v1/checkout-sessions/:token/pay
extra.conflict: The driver assumed every currency has two decimals, so a zero-decimal or three-decimal currency was charged or matched at the wrong amount.
extra.decision: Lead record (feature 24C, confirmed in review). Amounts in the Stripe protocol use a per-currency exponent table in both directions (to the gateway and back), rounding half up, never truncating: zero-decimal currencies, ISK and UGX (two decimals at the gateway, whole units only), and the three-decimal BHD, JOD, KWD, OMR and TND in steps of 0.010 (a last digit other than 0 is rounded at the gateway, e.g. JOD 3.396 charges 3.400, and the payment is held for staff by the exact mismatch guard; 3.505 becomes 3510). The warning is logged for a rounded outgoing amount. Owner default: configure those currencies with 2 display decimals in the console's currencies page so shown and charged amounts are always equal; no code forces it. Gateway calls gain an optional timeoutMs (default 10 s). Test gateways default to http://127.0.0.1:9 so tests never reach Stripe.

extra.conflict: B82 (refund results) says a refund completes on refund.succeeded, which Stripe does not send; the payments webhook ignored dispute events; card details (country, funding, fingerprint) were not read before capture.
extra.decision: Lead record (feature 24C; corrects B82, whose text should say refund.updated). Refund results come from refund.updated by its status and from refund.failed; refund.succeeded is not an event. A refund that fails late after it completed is noted on the refund, once, only when the gateway refund id matches the one it completed with (a canceled refund's failure text is 'canceled'); nothing is reversed in the ledger and there is no automatic re-open or re-send. POST /webhooks/payments/:gateway now also handles dispute events (answer { received: true }, 'duplicate' as the dispute handler says), next to POST /webhooks/disputes/:gateway. Before capture the card details are read from the PaymentIntent's latest Charge (3 second timeout, never throws, with a metric): unavailable details add a risk signal on a storefront payment and force staff review on a card top-up instead of crediting itself. A reference without the pi_ prefix, a charge with no card, or a successful intent without latest_charge counts as 'no details', not 'unavailable'. The card's country and funding type are not passed to risk (inputs cardCountry and prepaidCard exist; turning them on changes who is held, so the owner decides).

extra.conflict: A gateway kept one webhook secret, so rotating it at the gateway meant a window in which every webhook failed verification, and the console could not show which secret was stored.
extra.decision: Lead record (feature 24C). A gateway keeps up to two webhook secrets in the existing encrypted column (stored as a JSON list; legacy plain values are still read; no migration, same AAD), and both webhook endpoints accept a delivery signed with either. Wire (additive): responses carry webhookSecretHint and secondaryWebhookSecretHint (four bullets plus the last 4 characters, or null); POST and PATCH accept webhookSecret (write-only, replaces the first and keeps the second) and secondaryWebhookSecret (write-only; a string of 1 to 500 characters sets it, null removes it; a second secret without a first is 422 on 'secondaryWebhookSecret' with the field code requires_first). Values are never returned or audited; the audit snapshot gains the flag hasSecondaryWebhookSecret and 'secret changed' is true when any of the three was sent. Rotation as staff do it: put the new secret in 'second', roll the endpoint at the gateway, then save it as the first and remove the second. Owner question D-6 (keep Stripe through a foreign entity or build a local driver) stays open; the crypto driver stays off.

extra.conflict: The site had two forms, one for merchants (/client/auth/login) and one for customers, so a visitor had to know which kind of account they had. The new route is not in the map.
extra.decision: Lead record (feature 24A; customers module; a map addition, no successStatus because the console never calls it). One form for both kinds. Request { email (1 to 254), password (1 to 1024) }; answer 200 { kind: 'merchant' | 'customer', next: 'password' | 'totp' | 'done' } with Cache-Control no-store, the session and CSRF cookies of that kind, and the header X-CSRF-Token set to the token of that kind's surface. next: merchant password (temporary password, B193), totp (POST /client/auth/2fa) or done; customer password (POST /store/v1/me/password) or done. A merchant's email always signs in as the merchant; if the same email is also a customer and only the customer password matches, the answer is the same 401 (the customer area opens through the emailed sign-in link). Exactly one password verify per attempt, and both the merchant and the customer counters and the customer per-email lock are charged and read on every attempt before any lookup, so neither a 429 nor timing reveals which kind an email is. Protection: Turnstile always (X-Turnstile-Token, checked first), exact Origin check (403 CSRF_FAILED), no session or CSRF token needed, 'ip' limiter plus the 5 per 15 minutes per email and IP 'sign-in' limiter. Errors: 422 VALIDATION_FAILED, 401 UNAUTHORIZED (unknown email, wrong password, no password yet, anonymized: one answer), 403 ACCOUNT_SUSPENDED (only after a correct password), 403 TURNSTILE_FAILED, 403 IP_NOT_ALLOWED, 429 RATE_LIMITED with Retry-After. Signing in as one kind never signs the other kind out: only the stale session of the same kind is ended. No audit. The two old login routes stay public (the API recipe and existing clients use them). Recorded gap: POST /client/auth/login has no per-email lock of its own (it lives in the customers module, which identity cannot import), so a rotating-IP attacker can avoid the lock by using the old route; this needs a follow-up decision. The risk blocklist on merchant registration is not done.

extra.route: POST /client/auth/register, POST /client/auth/login, POST /client/auth/password/forgot (and every public /client route that opts in)
extra.conflict: Turnstile guarded only the storefront; ACCESS.client had no 'public with Turnstile' value, so the merchant sign-up, sign-in and password reset could not be protected, and the map's row flags could not add one.
extra.decision: Lead record (feature 24A; decision 034 amended). Turnstile may now guard public /client routes: ACCESS.client gains 'عام + Turnstile', and map additions gain rowFlags (add-only Turnstile flags on existing public rows, never a new row or a change to the map). The three merchant routes above are flagged; the check is enforced only while TURNSTILE_MERCHANT_AUTH=true (default false, to be set before go-live, once the site sends X-Turnstile-Token), and then a missing or bad token is 403 TURNSTILE_FAILED before anything else; with false they behave exactly as before. The contract and OpenAPI show X-Turnstile-Token as optional on those routes, with the extension x-gsm-turnstile-rollout, so the storefront's generated types keep working; TURNSTILE_FAILED and its metric text now cover both forms (metric name unchanged). Remove turnstileRollout and TURNSTILE_MERCHANT_AUTH one release after production runs with it on (the header then becomes required). X-Turnstile-Token is not added to the CORS allow list: topology A (B210) is same-origin.

extra.route: All browser-facing routes by host: SHOP_HOST (/client/*, /store/v1/*), ADMIN_HOST (/admin/*, /health, /reference*), API_HOST (/api/index.php, /v1/*, /webhooks/*, /docs*); decision 036
extra.conflict: Session cookies are host-only and SameSite=Lax, so a browser page and the API it calls must share one origin; nothing said which host serves which surface in production.
extra.decision: Lead record (decision 036, topology A: one browser origin per audience). SHOP_HOST serves the storefront and Caddy sends /client/* and /store/v1/* to the API on the same host; ADMIN_HOST serves the console and sends /admin/*, /health and /reference* to the API; API_HOST serves only the machine surfaces (/api/index.php, /v1/*, /webhooks/*, /docs*) and answers 404 elsewhere. /metrics is routed on no host. Result: no CORS preflight, no CORS change for X-Turnstile-Token, CSRF_COOKIE_DOMAIN stays unset and no cookie crosses hosts; a separate API host for browsers (topology B) is not built. Client address: only Caddy publishes ports; it sets X-Forwarded-For itself, the compose network has the fixed subnet 172.30.0.0/24 and TRUST_PROXY=172.30.0.0/24, so the API trusts exactly Caddy (and the forwarded header the storefront passes on its server-side calls); no trusted_proxies unless a CDN is put in front. Nothing here changes a route, a table or a response.

extra.route: CLI and deploy files (no HTTP route); SENTRY_DSN; decisions 015, 027 and 036
extra.conflict: The backend ran only from a developer checkout: no images, no deploy order, no backups, and error reporting was undecided.
extra.decision: Lead record (decision 036). One backend image, three commands: the API (default), the worker (bun src/worker.ts) and the one-off migrate (bun scripts/db-migrate.ts); the first run is bun run setup (see the P4b first-run entry). The API never migrates on boot (decision 027): a deploy is backup, build, run --rm migrate, up -d api worker, and rollback is the previous image tag, never a down-migration. The stack keeps the two Redis roles of decision 006 (queue: AOF everysec, noeviction; cache: allkeys-lru, no persistence); the worker has stop_grace_period 30s (its drain is 25 s). Backups: nightly pg_dump encrypted with age (private key offline) to a separate bucket, 30 daily and 12 monthly; a never-deleting copy of the files bucket (rclone copy, never sync); a scripted restore and a monthly drill that checks the ledger sums to zero and the migrations match; the queue Redis, cache Redis and Prometheus history are not backed up. Sentry is wired but off until SENTRY_DSN is set (decision 015). One host and one Postgres, no high availability: recovery is a restore from backup.

extra.conflict: The map gives services the columns min_qty, max_qty and qty_options but no body for the admin routes, and neither the console's assumed contract nor the backend's took or sent them, so every service sold exactly one per order.
extra.decision: Lead record (feature 25, owner request of 2026-11-11). The rows send, and POST and PATCH accept, minQty and maxQty (whole, 1 to 100000) and qtyOptions (at most 50 whole pack sizes from 1 to 100000, no repeats, stored ascending). A service sells a range or packs: with packs the server stores minQty as the smallest and maxQty as the largest pack, and refuses a sent minQty or maxQty that disagrees (422 packs_set); without packs maxQty under minQty is 422 on the key that was sent. PATCH changes only the keys sent; qtyOptions [] clears the packs. Pack problems are reported on the field qtyOptions. A CHECK (services_qty_limits_check) keeps the limits; order and uniqueness are the server rule's. The existing service audit rows carry the three values. No cache key: the catalog version already moves on every service write.

extra.conflict: The import created every service as one per order although a Dhru supplier states QNT, MINQNT, MAXQNT and QNTOPTIONS.
extra.decision: Lead record (feature 25). The four fields are read from the synced entry (supplier_services.raw; no new column) and normalised to a rule the catalog accepts, always a subset of the supplier's (unreadable values fall back to one per order; at most the 50 smallest packs; 100000 at most). The rule is written only when the import creates a service; a later import, sync or supplier change never overwrites a service's quantities. The preview shows the supplier's rule per item and quantityDiffers for a linked service whose rule is another one. An order's quantity is sent to the supplier as before.

openQuestions.topic: Fixed custom prices when the supplier cost rises
openQuestions.question: A merchant's custom price is fixed; when the supplier raises its price, how do we avoid selling below cost without overcharging the merchant silently? (raised by the user from a merchant conversation)
openQuestions.default: Order-time floor = cost + minimum profit on services.cost only (it changes when the admin imports the supplier's changed items).
openQuestions.answer: Floor uses max(service cost, latest synced supplier price); dashboard alert; the real price in imeiservicelist; import unchanged. An order whose price is more than a configurable tolerance (default 10%) above the merchant's last listed price is refused with PRICE_CHANGED (Dhru message: refresh the service list); within the tolerance the new price is charged and the order records the raise. Merchants who used a service in the last 30 days are notified (email, Telegram, webhook) when its price changes. Full rule: MISMATCHES B117.
